sourceWindows: CURRENT / INDEPENDENT TECHNO COMPILATION: https://stanprac.bandcamp.com/album/out-of-practice-vol-2 — all 15 named tracks on the forthcoming 2026-10-01 digital compilation were screened, including the two already streamable tracks and the label's track-specific highlights. Stave & Grebenstein — Live Room retained because the label compares this exact collaboration to a Pan Sonic/DAF encounter; the vinyl edition is dated 2026-09-07.

CURRENT / BERLIN TECHNO: https://frameworksmusic.bandcamp.com/album/evolution-ep — all four tracks on Decka's 2026-01-16 Evolution EP were screened. Obscure Arcade Game retained as the least literal structural hypothesis inside the release's independently attributed pulsing, chaotic techno frame; that description applies to the EP, not the track alone.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / TEXTURAL TECHNO: https://ra.co/reviews/33498 and https://tomvr.bandcamp.com/track/fast-track-to-bliss — Fast Track To Bliss retained because the exact-track review documents a kick that begins as an afterthought and doubles toward the end, while bass, delayed synths and voice carry the structure.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / HYBRID OUTSIDER CLUB: https://ra.co/reviews/35275 and https://jaymiesilk.bandcamp.com/album/rub-music-vol-1-artificial-realness — all six tracks were screened. Mechanical Bird retained because the review describes fractious beats and polyrhythms followed by a reboot from melody-stripped IDM into disjointed PC music.

ADDITIONAL CURRENT WINDOWS: https://unterwegsrecs.bandcamp.com/album/unterwegs-ix-anika-kunst-the-power-of-presence and https://tomvr.bandcamp.com/album/dont-know-how-fast-im-moving-until-i-hit-something-2 — nine released or previewed tracks were screened. No exact track was promoted because the strongest descriptions were release-level or listener comments rather than track-specific editorial evidence.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 38 named tracks across two current techno releases, two overlooked catalogue releases and two additional current windows; metadata and attributed descriptions only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–61 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.

Anika Kunst and current Tom VR album tracks were not elevated from release-level framing or listener comments. Decka's pulsing/chaotic description is explicitly retained as release-level rather than falsely attributed to Obscure Arcade Game.

No lead was promoted for recency, artist or label reputation, genre, novelty, title, or structural cleverness. BPM, energy, density, space, hypnosis, emotional effect, phrase structure, harmonic relation and mixability remain unknown unless explicitly stated.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Jaymie Silk — Mechanical Bird: strongest exact structural-freedom case, with documented fractious polyrhythms and a mid-track stylistic reboot.
2. Tom VR — Fast Track To Bliss: strongest gradual internal-development case, with exact-track evidence that the kick doubles late rather than governing the opening.
3. Stave & Grebenstein — Live Room: strongest current industrial collaboration hypothesis, supported by a track-specific Pan Sonic/DAF comparison but without detailed rhythmic evidence.
4. Decka — Obscure Arcade Game: current exact identity from a pulsing, chaotic techno EP; evidence is release-level and therefore weaker.
